prior_amendment.role: S41 recorded the measured fact once, in reading only; this amendment records the corrected basis, the defect in the runner, and the new enforcement code

amends.rule: the pre-registration is not edited. This amendment records the actual sample basis and the defect, and registers the enforcement that a future total cap must use.

finding.what_was_registered: the anchored-subset registration says the intermediate pass caps MMLU at 2,000 items and calls that 'total items; the same stratified first-2000 the harness selects under a fixed seed'. It calls the knowledge mean an estimate on 2,000 of 14,042.
finding.what_was_actually_scored: all 14,042 MMLU items in every arm. MMLU is a 57-subject group task and lm-evaluation-harness applies `limit` per subtask, not to the group total. `--limit-map mmlu=2000` therefore selected min(2000, n_subject) for every subject; every subject has fewer than 2,000 items, so the effective sample was the full set.

measured_evidence.reading: a true 2,000-item run would be about one seventh of the anchor's full-MMLU wall time; 654 s against 639 s is the full set, and the receipt's own `sample_len` says 14,042

defect.class: the runner passed a total-item intention to a per-subtask parameter; the harness had no way to know the intention
defect.registration_text_status: `anchored_subset.tasks.mmlu.limit = 2000` and `limit_semantics = total items` remain written in the pre-registration because that file is not edited. They are superseded by this amendment's stated basis.
defect.runner_status: the receipts record what was run (`pre_registered.limit = 2000`, `limit_from_limit_map = true`) beside what was scored (`n_samples.sample_len = 14042`); the receipt is read that way

mmlu.basis_identity: the same basis as the anchor's 37.90 knowledge mean and the registered 42.01 knowledge threshold

enforcement.why_new_code: scripts/s40_score.py was executing when this was written and must not be edited during a pass; the new driver does not modify it
enforcement.mechanism: the harness exposes exact sample selection through `simple_evaluate(samples={leaf: [indices]})`, so a group total cap is expressed as a largest-remainder allocation of the requested total over the group's leaves. The allocation is deterministic, the per-leaf lengths sum to exactly the requested total, and the driver refuses a cap smaller than the leaf count.
enforcement.receipt_field: `total_cap_enforcement` records the requested cap, the allocation, the effective total read back from the harness's own `n-samples`, and `within_cap`
enforcement.fail_closed: the run raises if the effective total exceeds the requested cap; the receipt is not written as complete

self_test.command: SELVEDGE_MEM=6g SELVEDGE_CPUS=4 SELVEDGE_PIDS=256 SELVEDGE_TMP=1g scripts/court eval -- python3 scripts/s43_score_total_cap.py --self-test
self_test.measured: mmlu leaves = 57, full total = 14,042, a 2,000-item total cap allocates exactly 2,000, the allocation is deterministic, and a cap below the leaf count fails closed

enforcement.no_rerun: the existing MMLU receipts are already on the full 14,042-item basis, so the defect changed the reading, not the data. Any future MMLU subset must use the new driver; it may not re-use `--limit-map` as if it were a total cap.

related_provenance_fix.question: why the stage-2 base differs from the anchor base on the same checkpoint
related_provenance_fix.cause: CONFIG DIFFERENCE: the anchor loads the checkpoint through HFLM with the transformers default attention (measured `sdpa`); the stage-2 loader passed `attn_implementation='eager'`. Prompts, targets, task configs, limits, batch sizes, seeds, lm_eval and transformers versions, model revision and harness commit are identical.

item_level.mmlu_pro: 504 items; 156 generations differ; 139 vs 135 correct; 16 anchor-correct/stage-2-wrong and 12 the other way
item_level.minerva_math500: 500 items; 220 generations differ; math_verify 117 vs 125; 9 anchor-correct/stage-2-wrong and 17 the other way
item_level.gsm8k: 1,319 items; 436 generations differ; strict-match 512 vs 514; 30 and 32 the other way

related_provenance_fix.fix: oracle/frontier/arms.py now takes `attn_implementation` and omits it when None; scripts/s40_compare.py's eval backbone uses the anchor default and records `eval_attention_implementation` in the arm report. The held-out instrument keeps its previous eager path. The two historical receipts are not edited; the next base score is the one to compare to the anchor.

what_this_amendment_does_not_establish: that a 2,000-item MMLU estimate equals the full MMLU score: it is an estimate, and the existing receipts are the full set
that the stage-2 base and the anchor base measure different model states: the weights are identical and the difference is the attention kernel
that the attention kernel difference explains every future score difference: it explains the measured generation divergence here; it is not a licence to ignore other config changes
that any arm's family mean should be compared to the 42.01 / 39.27 thresholds as a win: the intermediate pass still draws no win verdict
